text.p: Australian Resources Minister Warwick Parer said on Monday the government had issued a production licence to Woodside Petrolum Ltd to develop the Laminaria and Corallina oil fields in the Timor Sea.
Parer said the development of the oil fields would cost A$1.08 billion.
Parer said the two fields were currently estimated to have combined recoverable oil reserves of up to 250 million barrels.
A spokesman for Parer estimated production from the oilfields would be worth about A$7 billion, but did not say over what period.

"Australia's self-sufficiency in oil will be boosted by up to 20 percent when production commences in 1999," he said in a statement. "This will result in a net improvement in Australia's annual balance of payments of up to $1.8 billion."
Parer said the project had been designed for maximum production of 170,000 barrels a day.
The combined oilfields had an estimated life of 14 years, he said.
Woodside Petroleum owns 50 percent of the joint venture while Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd and Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd each hold 25 percent.
